summary.one_liner: A device-tested guide and toolkit for running Claude Code natively on Android through three install paths (Termux, proot-Ubuntu, and the Android Virtualization Framework), with a verification harness, per-device results, and security guidance.
summary.what_it_does: The repository provides installation scripts and documentation for running the Claude Code CLI on an Android phone without root or a cloud VM. Path A (Native Termux) uses an install script that sets up a Termux compatibility layer and a launcher that checks for new Claude Code versions daily, keeps a backup version, and can roll back after a detected startup crash. Path B runs Ubuntu inside Termux via proot-distro and installs Claude Code with Anthropic's own installer, at a cost of roughly 2 GB of storage. Path C targets phones with Android's Linux development environment option and runs a Debian VM through AVF. The README also covers a pinned fallback install for Android 8 to 10 devices, device compatibility results from specific phones, troubleshooting and recovery steps, and a security model describing prompt injection, storage and ADB risks, and the DNS resolver change. It also documents example uses such as geofence alerts, voice chat through a Termux skill, and notification triage. The README mentions an SSRF-guard WebFetch hook, a biometric approval gate, and a verification harness in its description, but the README body itself does not detail them.
use_cases: Run Claude Code on an Android phone without root
Set up a Linux environment with Claude Code inside Termux
Choose between Termux, proot Ubuntu, and AVF install paths
Check whether a specific Android phone can run Claude Code
Recover or roll back a broken Claude Code install on Android
Review security risks before giving an AI agent access to phone files and ADB
how_to_run: Install Termux from F-Droid or GitHub (not Google Play) on a 64-bit phone
Open Termux and download install.sh with curl -fsSL -o install.sh <url> (the URL is not given in the README)
Open a new Termux session and run: claude
On Android 8, 9, or 10, use install-pinned.sh instead of install.sh, or use Path B
Path B and Path C are separate guides linked from the README
notable: Three distinct install paths, from a lightweight Termux setup to a full Linux VM via AVF
Auto-update launcher that keeps a previous version as backup and tries saved versions after a startup crash
Per-device test results and a call for community device reports
Security-focused documentation with a threat model and a list of start-safe practices
Author describes running voice mode on Android by building a microphone module for Termux, with two pull requests to Termux upstream
caveats: Path A is not an official Anthropic Android build; it runs Anthropic's Linux version through a Termux compatibility layer
Path A's launcher cannot recover without a usable saved version and cannot catch every failure during use
Path A sets the DNS resolver to Google's 8.8.8.8 and 8.8.4.4 by default, bypassing a local DNS server such as Pi-hole
Path C is labeled experimental and is tested on only a few devices
Android 8 to 10 phones can only use the pinned older Claude Code 2.1.112 fallback; the maintainer states the project is maintained alone
